title: While We Were Still Sinners
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: You don't need to clean yourself up before you come to Jesus. Run to him, and see how much more is yours through his life.
exhortation: While we were weak and while we were sinners, Jesus chose to come and die. That shows us we don't need to clean ourselves up before we come to him. We don't need to have a good week, make up for it, or stack up good deeds first. We should run all the faster when we find ourselves in need and in our sin.

The prodigal son decided to go back to his father at the lowest point of his life, and so should we. Maybe you're in a dark place right now. Maybe you feel guilty and weighed down by your sin. The best thing you can do is run to Jesus. While we were still sinners, Christ died for us. He didn't wait for us to get our act together.

And look at the glorious future in this passage: "much more shall we be saved by his life." If we are saved from our sin through his death, how much more will we receive through his life? The future he has given us in Christ is more than we can imagine. He didn't just save us, give us a clean slate, and say, "Now you're on your own." He has given us his righteousness. Everything Christ deserves, we receive, because he received what we deserve.
prayer: Lord, thank you for pursuing us when we were dead in our sins and trespasses, without any hope. A dead man can't make himself alive. You breathed life into dead souls, called us out of the grave, and made us new creations with new hearts to follow hard after you.
So may we follow hard after you, Lord Jesus. Amen.
